producer_report.summary: The baseline stage now reuses a green GitHub run for the base's governed content instead of running fmt, clippy and test locally. Otherwise it runs locally as before. `take_baseline` calls the new `reused_baseline`, which makes at most two reads of the host and runs no check. It uses the candidate-path calls `routing::route` (config kind, so no path skipping), `run_routed_with_record` and `ci_result::resolve`. A refusing executor and a source that never reads logs mean a miss never runs anything and never fails the job. (1) Find the commit the host has: step over commits that change only `records/` (the job's own prediction commit is one, the host has never seen it), up to 20 commits. (2) Landed candidate's run: take the one added `verification.json` in that squash. Reuse the run of its `candidate_commit` on the previous job's CI branch only if the recorded fingerprint equals `fingerprint(base, base)`. The squash's changed paths go to `resolve`, so a workflow edit is refused. (3) Main's run: the push run for that commit on the default branch from the local `origin/HEAD`, only if its governed content equals the base's. A hit stores a baseline with `reused_from` (the run address) and every check marked reused and passed. It prints `ci         baseline reused from <run> for <base>`. A miss prints `ci         baseline runs locally: <reason>`. Nested runs and repositories with no GitHub origin print nothing new. `Baseline.reused_from` is optional, defaulted and not written when empty, so old files parse and local-baseline files are unchanged. CHANGELOG and the `ci_result` module doc describe it. I did not run the whole workspace suite; Athena runs it.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs (run with `cargo test -p athena-core baseline`) gives a green CI result for the base's fingerprint. `take_baseline` returns a baseline marked reused, whose checks are marked reused and pass, and the local check executor was never invoked.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core baseline_` passes baseline_reused_from_the_landed_candidates_run_runs_nothing_locally and baseline_reused_from_the_default_branch_run_runs_nothing_locally. Both run through Athena::go with a baseline command that leaves a marker file `baseline-ran` outside the job directory, so it survives the job-directory cleanup. They assert the stored baseline.json has reused_from == Some(CI_RUN_ADDRESS), note None, checks fmt/clippy/test each reused and passed with a note naming the CI run and sha, the marker absent, and the `ci         baseline reused from <run> for <base>` line. The landed-candidate test also asserts exactly one baseline read, for head_sha=<previous candidate> on branch athena/ci/<previous job>.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test (run with `cargo test -p athena-core baseline`) has no CI result, a red one, or a lookup error for the base's fingerprint. `take_baseline` runs the checks locally as before and returns the same records as before, with no reuse marker, and a red or error case also leaves a note.
criteria_check.evidence: baseline_runs_locally_when_no_green_ci_result_exists passes. It loops over: no run, red run, unfinished run, unreachable host (runner returns Err), different recorded fingerprint, a landing that edited a workflow file (with a green run), a landing of two jobs, and a no-origin control. In each case the marker exists (the checks ran here), reused_from is None, note is None, and the checks are fmt/clippy/test with reused false. With a GitHub origin there is exactly one `ci         baseline runs locally: <reason>` line holding the case's words (the red case names the run address, the unreachable case says no usable CI result). With no origin there is no `ci         baseline` line. Departure: the 'note' is this output line, not Baseline.note; see open_issues.

criteria_check.criterion: The `Baseline` round-trip tests in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, via `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord::Baseline` on `{job}/baseline.json`, pass with and without the new reuse field. An older baseline file with no such field still parses (`cargo test -p athena-data`).
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-data baseline` passes 8 tests, including a_baseline_written_before_reuse_existed_still_parses_with_no_source (no key serialised, check_record_file ok, parses to None), a_reused_baseline_round_trips_and_validates (Some round-trips, check_record_file ok, excuses nothing as pre-existing) and a_baseline_with_an_unknown_key_is_still_refused.

I ran clippy --all-targets --locked -D warnings (clean), fmt --check (clean), the athena-core lib suite (902 passed), athena-data baseline tests, the drain integration tests (164 passed) and the policy test; I did not run the full workspace `cargo test`.

criteria_check.criterion: Reuse is keyed on the same governed-content fingerprint that candidate check reuse uses, through the existing `ci_result::resolve` path, not a new lookup. The reuse decision and its reason (reused from which run, or why it ran locally) are printed in the job's output like the existing `ci         checks reused from ...` line.
criteria_check.evidence: `green_run` in run/checks.rs calls `routing::run_routed_with_record`, which calls `ci_result::resolve`, inside `with_ci_source_on`. No lookup function was added to ci_result.rs. The fingerprint compared is `fingerprint(&self.git, base, base)`, the call candidate.rs uses for base_fingerprint. The reuse test lines assert `ci         baseline reused from <run> for <base>`; the fallback test asserts `ci         baseline runs locally: <reason>` per case.

open_issues: Departure from criterion 2's wording: a fallback leaves its reason on the output line `ci         baseline runs locally: <reason>`, not in Baseline.note. `Baseline::failed_before` and `failed_tests_before` return nothing when `note` is set, so a note would stop real pre-existing failures from being excused. That would change the verdict rules, which are out of scope.

Departure from the plan: the plan took the base's single parent as the landing squash. In `go`, `ctx.prediction` is a records-only commit that Athena makes on top of the current head (`commit_records`), which the host has never seen. So the code first steps over commits that change only `records/` (at most 20) to the content commit, then uses that commit for both lookups. Lookup B also requires that commit's fingerprint to equal the base's. The tests reflect this: the squash helper adds a real content file, and the main-run test sets the fake for the commit under the job's records.

Host: does GitHub keep and return runs for an `athena/ci/<job>` branch after it is deleted at job close? If not, lookup A never hits live and only main's run (B) can save time. The tests use a fake and prove nothing about this.
Host: is `origin/HEAD` set in the clone Athena runs in? B is skipped when it is not, with the reason `origin/HEAD is not set` on the ci line.
Host: does the landing squash on this repository still carry the landed job's `records/jobs/.../verification.json` in main's tree? If not, A finds nothing and B alone applies.

Not on the brief's list but touched: crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs (one line, `reused_from: None` in a test literal, needed to compile) and crates/athena-core/src/reconcile.rs (one word: `local_default_branch` is now `pub(crate)` so the baseline lookup reuses it).

The baseline command in the new tests touches `../../baseline-ran`. The first version put the marker in the job directory, which is cleaned when the job closes, so the 'no local run' check would have passed vacuously; I caught that when the fallback test failed, and moved the marker outside.
mistakes: My first test marker lived in the job directory, which is removed when the job closes, so the local-run check was vacuous until the fallback test failed. Fixed by using a marker beside the job directory.
My first squash helper made a records-only commit, which the new records-only walk correctly skipped. It now adds a content file.
learnings: `Athena::go` commits a records-only prediction commit on the current branch, and that commit is the job's base (`ctx.prediction`). The host has never seen it, so any host lookup for the base has to start from the commit under it.

`check_seam` only fakes the candidate's checks (`SnapExec`). The baseline always runs its real command through `baseline_runs`. A marker file written by the baseline command is the way to observe a local baseline run in tests.
A job directory is removed when the job closes, so a test must look for a marker beside it, not inside it.
Closing records under `records/` are excluded from the governed-content fingerprint; the squash helper asserts this.
On disk, records are `AnyRecord` JSON, so they are read with `AnyRecord::parse`, not as the bare struct.
Bash here cannot pipe or use `tail`, and tool-result files outside the working directory cannot be read. Use `-q` or `--message-format short` to keep cargo output small.
desires: A job-level hook to observe whether the baseline command ran, as `check_seam` does for the candidate's checks.
An intermediate-test-result file readable inside the working directory, so long cargo output could be inspected without rerunning.
